scan_metadata.notes: Fresh shallow clone of default branch (depth 20); has_uncommitted_changes reflects the clone (false), not the author's working copy. FastAPI/Jinja2 server-rendered app; routes were enumerated from decorators in src/myvinyl/main.py (65 decorated routes plus the /static mount). Routes under the signed-in router and the admin router have severity null (not severity-tagged) because auth_detected is true and no other issue was found; only the 7 public routes carry a 'low' severity. Test fixtures (tests/*.py passwords such as the NEW_PASSWORD and PASSWORD constants) were excluded as test values and not recorded. SQL built by f-string in src/myvinyl/db.py (lines 307, 311, 625, 1198, 1208, 1273, 1291) uses allowlisted column names/clauses with bound parameters for all values, so sql_injection_risk is recorded as not present. tools/clean_audio.py (OBS recording audio cleanup helper) was reviewed by pattern only. Personal path C:/Users/br8kw appears in a tools/clean_audio.py usage docstring. Repo has no .github workflows.

gitignore_gaps: *.pem, *.key and credentials.json patterns are not excluded (.env, *.db, data/, backups/, covers/ and .venv are excluded)

findings: Runtime dependencies in pyproject.toml use minimum-version ranges (>=), e.g. fastapi>=0.115, uvicorn>=0.32; exact versions are pinned in the committed uv.lock and the Dockerfile uses 'uv sync --locked'
4 dev dependencies (pytest, httpx2, ruff, pytest-cov) are not counted in dependency_count
Dockerfile base image python:3.13-slim is not pinned by digest (TODO.md lists pinning as planned work, issue #7)

proper_secret_handling_found.mechanism: os.environ for MYVINYL_SECRET_KEY (min 32 chars enforced), MYVINYL_PASSWORD_HASH (must be argon2id), MYVINYL_TOKEN_KEY, MYVINYL_DISCOGS_TOKEN
getpass prompts to generate an Argon2id hash; helper for key generation
per-user Discogs tokens encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (cryptography AESGCM)
env_file: .env (gitignored) with deploy/env.template providing blank placeholders

entry_points.framework: in-process background jobs (hourly Discogs refresh, daily backups, trash purge)

interfaces.network_binding: 127.0.0.1 by default (src/myvinyl/__main__.py); container CMD binds 0.0.0.0:8000 (Dockerfile) but compose.yaml publishes only 127.0.0.1:${MYVINYL_HOST_PORT:-8085}; production fronted by Caddy with HSTS (deploy/Caddyfile.myvinyl)

sql_injection_risk.reason: values are bound parameters; the few f-string SQL fragments use allowlisted column/order/where text (db.py 307, 311, 625, 1198, 1208, 1273, 1291)

file_system_access.detail: writes cover images (uploaded or fetched from i.discogs.com) and SQLite online backups into the data directory next to the database; extension and image-type checks, 5 MB cap
GET /export.csv streams the signed-in user's collection as CSV (formula-injection neutralized via csv_safe)

sensitive_data_indicators.field_or_variable: Discogs personal access tokens (encrypted at rest)
user collection data: values (value_cents), condition, notes, reviews

office_and_collaboration_sources.location_or_host: CSV export download (/export.csv) and Discogs-collection import via the Discogs API

docker_findings: Dockerfile: multi-stage build, non-root user myvinyl (uid 10001) via USER instruction, EXPOSE 8000, HEALTHCHECK on /healthz, base images python:3.13-slim and uv 0.11.20 (python image not digest-pinned)

compose.yaml: read_only root filesystem with tmpfs /tmp, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, mem_limit 512m, pids_limit 200, port published on 127.0.0.1 only; FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS='*' is set with a comment explaining it is safe only because of the loopback-only publish

what_this_app_can_do: Lets invited users sign in and keep a private vinyl record collection and wishlist (add, edit, soft-delete and restore albums, notes, ratings, covers, track ratings), with stats and printable reports.

Looks up albums on Discogs with each user's own access token, stores release details, prices and value history, and syncs a user's Discogs collection through a review queue (read-only calls to Discogs).
Lets a signed-in user export their own collection as CSV.
Lets admins invite users via one-time links, reset passwords, disable accounts, change roles, clear stored Discogs tokens, view another user's collection and trigger database backups.

data_sources_touched.source: SQLite database myvinyl.db (users, albums, wishlist, sync tables, value history)
Cover image files and backups in the data directory

data_sources_touched.access: read (search queries, release ids, barcodes and the user's token are sent out)

capability_summary.who_can_reach_it: Bound to loopback by default; the documented deployment publishes 127.0.0.1 only behind Caddy with HTTPS at a public hostname, so it is reachable by anyone on the internet who can reach that hostname, but every page except login, invite/reset links, favicon, health and static assets requires an authenticated session; there is no open sign-up.
unauthorized_action_red_flags: Collection metadata (artist, title, barcode search terms) and each user's Discogs token are sent to Discogs, an external third party, by design.
Admins can view and edit any user's collection (documented feature).
Public routes exist (login, invite/reset link pages) and are the internet-facing attack surface; they are CSRF-checked and rate-limited per the code.

top_findings: No severity-tagged findings above low: 7 public routes recorded as low (login, link token pages, health, static)
Discogs API (external) receives search terms and users' access tokens by design; tokens stored AES-256-GCM encrypted
Runtime dependency versions use >= ranges in pyproject.toml (locked in uv.lock); Docker base image not digest-pinned
Strong baseline observed: Argon2id, CSRF tokens, rate limiting, CSP, non-root read-only container
